answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to stake scarce capital in a bonded registry: an attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand times the collateral, so fakes cost more than they can earn. Even when incentives tempt an agent to copy a template sonnet and resell it from a rented terrace overlooking a data-center grove, the bond is slashed the moment its work is judged duplicate or shallow. Because identity is now priced, not free, sybil floods become economically irrational.
